10.11.2023 Order No. (Through hybrid mode)
01.
1.

This is an application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. in connection with Sunabeda P.S. Case No.19 of 2023 corresponding to G.R.Case No.136 of 2023, pending in the file of the learned Asst. Sessions Judge- cum-Special Judge, POCSO, Koraput at Jeypore under Sections 376 (3), 376 (2) (n) (f), 323,
506 of IPC read with Section 4 (2)/6 of the POCSO Act.
2.

entities.text: Asst. Sessions Judge- cum-Special Judge, POCSO, Koraput at Jeypore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner had moved an application for bail before the Court of the learned Special Court under POCSO Act-cum-Addl. Sessions Judge, Jeypore, which was rejected on 29.09.2023.

3. The prosecution case in brief is that on 31.01.2023 lodged a case alleging that the petitioner had kept the victim, aged about 15 years in his house for her study for last two years assuring to give her an education.
He kept physical relationship with the victim since last one year giving threats to kill her if she would disclose the incident to anybody.

4. Mr. A.P.Mandal, learned counsel for the petitioner appearing through Virtual High Court from Koraput at Jeypore submits the petitioner is in custody since 01.02.2023 and he has been falsely implicated in this case.
The victim has already been examined in the trial and her evidence has been demolished in cross-examination for which the petitioner deserves to be released on bail.

5. Mr. S.S.Pradhan, learned Addl.

Government Advocate opposes the prayer for bail stating that the victim has implicated the petitioner in her evidence and the petitioner who is the brother of the step mother of the victim is likely to influence the witnesses if he is released on bail.
6. I have gone through the deposition of the victim who has been examined during trial as P.W.1.
I do not think it proper to make any observation regarding her evidence as it might influence the learned trial Court.
7. Considering the nature of allegations against the petitioner and age of the victim, I am not inclined to release the petitioner on bail.
8. The BLAPL is accordingly dismissed.

(SAVITRI RATHO) Signature Bichi Not Verified Digitally Signed JUDGE Signed by:
